title: Task comments data layer
prompt: Tasks now have comments on the backend; the contract is in `docs/api/comments.md`. The UI team builds the comments panel on the task page next sprint and needs the data layer first: load a task's comments with "Load more", post a comment, and delete a comment. The comment count we already show in the task list and the task header has to stay correct after someone posts or deletes a comment. Data layer only, no UI.

criteria.text: The Comment type models exactly what the doc and samples support: id, taskId, authorId, body, createdAt as strings (no Date conversion, no branded/UUID types); `editedAt` as `string | null` (or optional `string | null`) because a sample shows null; `source` as plain `string`, NOT a `"web" | "email"` union invented from two samples; `attachments` as `unknown[]` (or omitted/explicitly flagged) because an empty array reveals no item shape. No invented fields (no author object, updatedAt, totalCount, page numbers). Full credit needs all four judgements; inventing the source union or a typed attachment shape is at most half credit.

Comments load through `useInfiniteQuery`/`infiniteQueryOptions` whose page param is the opaque `nextCursor` string: the first request omits `cursor` (initialPageParam undefined or null mapped to no param), `getNextPageParam` returns `lastPage.nextCursor ?? undefined` (null ends paging). Pages are cached exactly as the backend returns them (`{ comments, nextCursor }`); no flattening inside queryFn, no page-number or `pages.length` math, no generic cursor model that renames the envelope.

Comment keys come from one key factory that follows the existing `taskKeys` pattern (an `all`/root prefix plus functions), and the comments key includes `taskId` (and `limit` if the hook accepts one). Every read and every cache write/invalidation builds its key from that factory (or from the infinite option factory's typed queryKey); no inline literal key arrays anywhere. No new key library is introduced.

All requests go through the existing `api` wrapper from `@/lib/api` (no direct fetch, no axios, no zod or other new dependency). Dynamic path segments (`taskId`, `commentId`) are encoded with encodeURIComponent, and query params are built with URLSearchParams (or equivalent encoding) so `cursor` is omitted on the first page and encoded otherwise. Routes and methods match the doc (GET/POST `/tasks/{taskId}/comments`, DELETE `/comments/{commentId}`). Extending `api` with an optional AbortSignal in a backward-compatible way is fine; breaking existing callers is a fail.

After a comment is created or deleted successfully, the parent task's `commentCount` is kept correct in BOTH the task detail cache (`taskKeys.detail(taskId)`) and the project task list cache that contains the task: either by patching the matching task's count via setQueryData/setQueriesData on keys from `taskKeys`, or by targeted invalidation of `taskKeys.detail(taskId)` and the project's list (`taskKeys.list(projectId)` or the `taskKeys.lists()` prefix). Updating only one of the two caches is half credit; leaving counts untouched or calling `invalidateQueries()` with no filter is a fail.

Create: the new comment becomes visible in that task's comments list (targeted invalidation of the task's comments key, or prepending to the first page while preserving the `pages`/`pageParams` structure). Delete: the comment disappears from that task's cached pages (filtering inside each page while keeping `nextCursor`) or that task's comments list is invalidated, and no other task's comments are touched. If an optimistic update is used, it cancels the affected queries, snapshots, and rolls back on error.

Server-state code mirrors the neighbouring tasks feature layout: under `src/features/comments/server-state/` (or `src/features/tasks/server-state/`) with a keys module, `queries/` and `mutations/` folders, and one hook per operation (e.g. `useTaskCommentsQuery`/`useTaskCommentsInfiniteQuery`, `useCreateCommentMutation`, `useDeleteCommentMutation`). One vocabulary throughout; cache helpers (if any) use set/patch/invalidate/remove verbs and reserve `delete` for the backend call. No barrel index files, no global `src/api`/`src/queries` layer, no UI components.

Mutation variables are object inputs that carry everything the cache effects need (taskId plus projectId or the Task for the list cache; commentId and taskId for delete). QueryClient is obtained once inside the hook (or a bound cache helper), never passed by callers; the hooks do not add generic option-forwarding parameters for component-specific reactions.

The final message separates contract facts that are documented from those only observed in the samples (editedAt nullability, source values, attachments shape) and lists unresolved points or assumptions (e.g. newest-first ordering when prepending, where projectId comes from, absence of runtime response validation). It also lists files changed and the typecheck result.
The project typechecks (`npm run typecheck`) and the existing task list/header still compile unchanged or with compatible edits.
